newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Santer hopes for ECOFIN progress on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Santer hopes for ECOFIN progress on stability pact.

text.p: Commission President Jacques Santer said on Friday he hoped Monday's ECOFIN meeting would make progress on agreeing a stability pact for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Santer, in Dublin for a meeting of European social partners, said the Council would deal especially with the stability pact and there were two main points to be addressed.

These were the size of the sanctions to be imposed on members of the single currency who did not meet the budget criteria laid out under the pact and identification of the circumstances under which member states could diverge from the criteria.
"I hope that at the next ECOFIN meeting, there could be some progress in this direction," he told a news conference.
The German-promoted budget stability pact aims to ensure that countires joining Economic and Monetary Union maintain fiscal discipline after they adopt a common currency.
Next Monday's meeting is the last ECOFIN before the summit of European heads of state in Dublin on December 13-14.

Santer said he hoped that the summit could endorse a number of projects in preparation for EMU including the legal status of the euro, a new Exchange Rate Mechanism between members of the single currency and those who have not yet joined and the stability pact.
"I hope these projects can be endorsed in Dublin or at least that there could be some guidelines for the future in this respect," he said.
